summary: amazon.jobs `updated_time` tracks re-indexing, not posting, so it must never be presented as recency: show it beside `posted_date`, mark rows where they disagree, and give recency filters `posted_date` as their only source of truth.
reason: `updated_time` is a relative string ("about 21 hours") that reads as freshness but reflects the last touch of any kind, including re-indexing. Observed directly: reqs posted 2026-03-09, 2026-04-19 and 2026-05-18 each reported an updated_time of 9-14 hours. Prevalence is unstable rather than uniform — in a 1,532-req corpus only 7 of the 766 reqs older than 14 days read hours (400 correctly read "days"; the oldest, posted 2025-09-19, correctly read "10 months"), while a separate 1,000-req sample taken hours later the same day found the fresh-reading share far higher. Because the field is unreliable in both directions, it must never be the basis of a recency filter or sort; show it beside posted_date and mark disagreement instead.
validated_outcome: Live `find --country USA --sort relevant` marks reqs such as a May 14 2026 posting reporting "about 3 hours" updated; 11 of 40 sampled rows carried updated_diverged=true.
